notice: Python and libraries on this page: the page's own programs (the playground) run in your browser, in Python 3.13.2, while the research ran Python 3.14.6 on Linux with PyAutoGUI 0.9.54, PyScreeze 1.0.1, PyMsgBox 2.0.1, Pillow 12.3.0, NumPy 2.5.4, OpenCV 5.0.0.93 and pyperclip 1.11.0. A browser cannot move a mouse, press keys, take a screenshot of a screen or start the programs these examples need, so none of the 74 examples of the chapter runs here: every one is shown as recorded under Python 3.14.6, not run, each with its reason. Virtual display: every recorded program that moves the mouse, clicks, types or reads the screen ran against a private virtual X display (Xvfb) with real X clients, a local stand-in for a screen; the events were seen there and not on a real screen, and nobody saw the screen. The six pictures under six concepts were drawn or captured by the research programs on that virtual display; they were not made on this page. Windows, macOS and a real screen were never used. The deck, whose text is the Lecture tab, marks slides 5, 8, 14, 17, 22 and 23 NOT EXECUTED (slide 5: Windows, macOS, the accessibility permission of macOS and a real Wayland compositor; slide 8: a real second monitor and what a real desktop does with the hotkey ctrl, alt, delete; slide 14: HiDPI scaling and real or multiple monitors; slide 17: Windows and macOS window objects; slide 22: the Sushi Go Round game, a captcha and a real instant messenger; slide 23: Windows, macOS, a real screen, Python 3.15 final and the rest of the study's list), calls slides 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17, 19, 21, 22 and 23 Recorded (results of 13 October 2026 that it does not run again) and says on the slides that show a program that it ran on a virtual display, not a real screen.

recorded.LibraryVersion: This example reads the installed PyAutoGUI packages (their versions, their source files or the Python they accept) of the machine the research ran on; those packages are not in the browser's Python, whose platform is 'emscripten', a platform PyAutoGUI does not support. What it printed was seen on a virtual X display (Xvfb), not a real screen. It is shown as recorded under Python 3.14.6 and is not run on this page.

example_notes.pins: In your browser the Python is 3.13 and PyAutoGUI is not installed, so the checks of its version raise PackageNotFoundError; the slide printed (3, 14), True, True and, after importing pyautogui with no DISPLAY, KeyError: 'DISPLAY'.
